params.label: GNSS observations (GNSSRD)
params.what: The spacecraft's own GPS receiver measurements (Sentinel AUX_GNSSRD archives, .DBL or any RINEX 3 observation file). These are the measurements the orbit is determined from.
params.how: Add the files or folders covering at least the fitting arc before the cutoff. Several days can be added; only epochs inside the arc are used. 'Auto-select' picks matching files from the catalog.

params.label: GPS orbit & clock products
params.what: Where the GPS satellites were and what their clocks read: IGS Final, Rapid or Ultra-rapid (SP3 orbits + RINEX CLK clocks) and/or broadcast navigation (RINEX nav). At least one is required.
params.how: Add everything you have; the app chooses per epoch in the order Final > Rapid > Ultra-rapid > Broadcast, after excluding products not available at the cutoff (Forecast mode). Precise products give ~2-3 cm satellite orbits versus ~1 m for broadcast.

params.label: UTC cutoff
params.what: The moment the forecast is issued. Only measurements up to the cutoff are fitted, and the forecast starts at the cutoff.
params.how: Choose a time covered by your GNSSRD data. In Forecast mode nothing after this time is used (products, weather, EOP, attitude), so the result is an honest prediction.

params.label: Workflow
params.what: What to run: orbit determination from GNSS measurements followed by a forecast, or a plain propagation from one known state.
params.how: Use OD + Forecast for real operations. Use Propagate when you already have a state (typed, or from an OEM/POEORB) and want to study force models without fitting.

params.label: First cutoff date
params.what: First day of a window run. A window run repeats orbit determination and a forecast once per day, each day with its own cutoff and its own input files from the catalog.
params.how: The tested Sentinel-3A window starts on 2024-09-03. Press 'Run whole window' to process every day up to the last date; press '▶ Run' for the single cutoff above.

params.label: Last cutoff date
params.what: Last day of the window run (inclusive).
params.how: The tested window ends on 2024-11-02 (61 daily cutoffs). Each day needs observations and a GPS product in the catalog; days without data are listed as 'no data' and skipped.

params.label: Cutoff time of day
params.what: Time of day of every cutoff in the window.
params.how: 05:59:42 UTC is 06:00:00 GPS time in 2024 (GPS runs 18 s ahead of UTC); the tested window used it, so the six-hour arc covers GPS 00:00-06:00 of each day.

params.label: Days between cutoffs
params.what: Spacing of the cutoffs in the window run.
params.how: 1 = every day (the tested set). Use 7 for a quick weekly overview: about 9 runs instead of 61.

params.label: Run name
params.what: Free label stored with the run and shown in the history.
params.how: Use something you will recognise later, e.g. 'S3A 16 Oct rapid vs broadcast'.

params.label: Product mode
params.what: Forecast: only GPS products (and weather/EOP/attitude) available at the cutoff are used, so the run is a true forecast. Reconstruction: the best data present is used even if it was published later; results are labelled retrospective.
params.how: Use Forecast for anything presented as prediction accuracy. Use Reconstruction to see the best orbit achievable after the fact or to compare product tiers.

params.label: Issue-time evidence
params.what: How a precise product's publication time is established for Forecast mode. Nominal latency assumes IGS's documented delays (Ultra-rapid: 3 h after its observed part ends; Rapid: 17 h after the day; Final: 18 days after). Verified requires real issue-time metadata.
params.how: Nominal latency is the practical default and is reported as an assumption. Choose Verified only if your archive records when each file arrived.

params.label: Force product tier
params.what: Automatic picks the best eligible product per epoch. Forcing a tier uses only that class, for comparisons.
params.how: Leave on Automatic for operations. Force Broadcast vs Rapid etc. to measure how much precise products improve the orbit.

params.label: Fitting arc
params.what: Length of the measurement window before the cutoff that the orbit is fitted to.
params.how: 4-12 h is typical for LEO. Longer arcs average out noise and constrain drag better, but a manoeuvre inside the arc spoils the fit and drag mismodelling grows with length. 6 h is a good default.

params.label: Observation sampling
params.what: Spacing of the GNSS epochs used for positioning and fitting.
params.how: 300 s is plenty for a 6 h arc and fast. 30-60 s adds more fixes (slightly less noise) at higher cost. Must divide evenly into the data rate.

params.label: Pseudorange sigma
params.what: Assumed 1-sigma noise of the ionosphere-free code measurement; sets the weight of each fix and the size of the formal covariance.
params.how: 2-5 m for dual-frequency code with broadcast orbits; 1-2 m with IGS products. Too small makes the covariance optimistic; the run reports a variance factor near 1 when this is right.

params.label: Covariance weighting
params.what: Weights each position fix by its geometry (PDOP) and the pseudorange sigma, instead of treating all fixes equally.
params.how: Keep on: poor-geometry fixes then count less, which is both more accurate and gives a meaningful covariance.

params.label: Max OD iterations
params.what: Upper limit on Gauss-Newton iterations of the batch least-squares fit. A run that has not converged issues no forecast.
params.how: Convergence normally takes 3-6 iterations; 12 leaves margin. Raising it rarely helps a fit that is not converging; check the data instead.

params.label: Min GPS satellites
params.what: Minimum satellites a GPS product must cover at an epoch to be selected for it (4 unknowns: position and clock).
params.how: Keep 4. Raising it to 5-6 rejects weak epochs at the cost of fewer fixes.

params.label: Max PDOP
params.what: Position dilution of precision limit; fixes with worse satellite geometry are rejected.
params.how: 4-6 is typical. Lower is stricter (fewer, better fixes).

params.label: Max SPP residual RMS
params.what: Rejects position fixes whose pseudorange residuals are larger than this, which usually means a bad measurement or satellite.
params.how: 10-30 m with broadcast orbits, 5-10 m with precise products.

params.label: Estimate drag coefficient
params.what: Solve for the drag coefficient Cd together with the orbit, instead of keeping it fixed.
params.how: Helps when drag dominates the error (low orbits, high solar activity) and the arc is long enough (>= 6-12 h). On short arcs it can be poorly determined and absorb noise.

params.label: Estimate radiation coefficient
params.what: Solve for the solar radiation pressure coefficient Cr.
params.how: Usually weakly observable over a few hours; leave off unless the arc spans many orbits and SRP matters (high area-to-mass).

params.label: Forecast / propagation span
params.what: How far ahead of the cutoff (or initial state) the orbit is predicted.
params.how: 7 days is the default; 14, 21 or 30 are one click away, or type any value. Errors grow with time mainly through drag; beyond a week the formal covariance and the uncertainty in solar activity dominate.

params.label: Output step
params.what: Time between ephemeris lines in the OEM file.
params.how: 60 s suits visualisation and interpolation (OEM declares Lagrange order 7). Use 10-30 s for precise users, 300 s for small files.

params.label: OEM reference frame
params.what: Frame of the positions/velocities written to the OEM.
params.how: EME2000 is the most widely read inertial frame. GCRF differs from it by ~23 mas (frame bias, ~1 m at LEO). ITRF is Earth-fixed, convenient for ground stations and maps.

params.label: Write formal covariance
params.what: Propagates the OD uncertainty forward and writes 6x6 covariance blocks into the OEM.
params.how: Costs one extra (simplified) propagation per estimated parameter. It is formal uncertainty from the measurement noise model, not a guarantee of actual error (drag and manoeuvres are not in it).

params.label: Covariance every N steps
params.what: Write a covariance block every N ephemeris lines.
params.how: 60 with a 60 s step gives hourly covariance, a good balance of detail and file size.

params.label: Object name
params.what: OEM OBJECT_NAME. Blank = taken from the GNSSRD file (e.g. SENTINEL-3A).
params.how: Leave blank for Sentinel files; set it for other spacecraft.

params.label: Object ID
params.what: OEM OBJECT_ID, normally the COSPAR international designator.
params.how: e.g. 2016-011A for Sentinel-3A. Blank = filled for known Sentinels, else UNKNOWN.

params.label: Mass
params.what: Spacecraft mass. Drag and radiation accelerations scale with area divided by mass.
params.how: Use the current mass including propellant. Only the ratios Cd*A/m and Cr*A/m matter, so an error in mass can be absorbed by estimating Cd.

params.label: Shape model
params.what: Cannonball: one constant area in every direction. Box-wing: a body box plus solar array whose projected area follows the attitude.
params.how: Cannonball is the generic default and is adequate when Cd is fixed or estimated. Box-wing is more physical for elongated spacecraft with large arrays and needs the plate areas.

params.label: Drag area
params.what: Cross-section facing the flow (cannonball model).
params.how: Average projected area; with Cd 2.2 typical LEO spacecraft have A/m of 0.005-0.02 m^2/kg.

params.label: Radiation area
params.what: Area facing the Sun (cannonball model).
params.how: Include the solar array, which usually dominates.

params.label: Drag coefficient Cd
params.what: How efficiently the thin upper atmosphere transfers momentum to the spacecraft.
params.how: 2.0-2.4 for most satellites; 2.2 is the standard assumption. Estimate it in the OD when drag dominates.

params.label: Radiation coefficient Cr
params.what: Fraction of sunlight momentum transferred: 1 = fully absorbed, 2 = perfect mirror.
params.how: 1.2-1.5 is typical.

params.label: Attitude source
params.what: Orientation used by the box-wing model: a nominal yaw-steering law, or measured quaternions from AUX_PROQUA files.
params.how: Nominal is within ~2 deg of measured for Sentinel-3 and needs no data. Measured attitude is used only up to the cutoff in Forecast mode.

params.label: Body face X area
params.what: Plate area of the box-wing model.
params.how: From the spacecraft's macro-model document (e.g. Sentinel-3 CPOD: X 2.84, Y 5.41, Z 6.10, array 10.5 m^2).

params.label: Body face Y area
params.what: Plate area of the box-wing model.
params.how: From the spacecraft's macro-model document (e.g. Sentinel-3 CPOD: X 2.84, Y 5.41, Z 6.10, array 10.5 m^2).

params.label: Body face Z area
params.what: Plate area of the box-wing model.
params.how: From the spacecraft's macro-model document (e.g. Sentinel-3 CPOD: X 2.84, Y 5.41, Z 6.10, array 10.5 m^2).

params.label: Solar array area
params.what: Plate area of the box-wing model.
params.how: From the spacecraft's macro-model document (e.g. Sentinel-3 CPOD: X 2.84, Y 5.41, Z 6.10, array 10.5 m^2).

params.label: Array cant angle
params.what: Tilt of the solar array relative to its rotation plane.
params.how: Sentinel-3: 24 deg.

params.label: Earth gravity field
params.what: Earth's non-spherical gravity (spherical harmonics). Off = central point mass only (two-body).
params.how: Always on for real work; switch off only to see how much the field matters.

params.label: Gravity degree
params.what: Highest spherical-harmonic degree used.
params.how: Effect saturates near degree 70-80 at 800 km. 20-40 is faster with small loss; bundled EGM96 stops at 70 (add an ICGEM file for more).

params.label: Gravity order
params.what: Highest order used (<= degree).
params.how: Normally equal to the degree. Order 0 keeps only the zonal terms (J2, J3...).

params.label: Atmospheric drag
params.what: Drag from the thin upper atmosphere; the dominant uncertainty for LEO prediction.
params.how: Always on below ~1000 km.

params.label: Density model
params.what: Thermosphere density model used for drag.
params.how: NRLMSISE-00 (default) was the most accurate at 1 day in the Sentinel-3A study. JB2008 responds better to geomagnetic storms (uses its bundled solar indices). Harris-Priester and exponential are fast, crude models for quick looks.

params.label: Solar radiation pressure
params.what: Push of sunlight, with Earth shadow (umbra/penumbra).
params.how: On for all real work; metre-level over a day.

params.label: Sun gravity
params.what: Third-body attraction of the Sun.
params.how: Keep on; tens of metres over a day.

params.label: Moon gravity
params.what: Third-body attraction of the Moon.
params.how: Keep on; tens of metres over a day.

params.label: Sun/Moon ephemeris
params.what: Source of Sun and Moon positions for third-body forces, radiation pressure and the density model.
params.how: Analytic (~0.01 deg) is the generic default. DE440 (add lnxp1990.440) is exact and slightly improves short-arc accuracy.

params.label: Solid Earth tides
params.what: Gravity change from the Earth's body tides.
params.how: Small (decimetres/day); keep on for precise work.

params.label: Ocean tides
params.what: Gravity change from ocean tides (FES2004, bundled).
params.how: Small (centimetres-decimetres/day).

params.label: General relativity
params.what: Schwarzschild correction to Earth's gravity.
params.how: Centimetre-level; keep on for precise work.

params.label: Lense-Thirring
params.what: Frame-dragging relativistic term.
params.how: Millimetre-level; harmless to keep on.

params.label: Earth albedo & infrared
params.what: Radiation pressure from sunlight reflected by Earth and its thermal emission.
params.how: Decimetre-level for LEO; keep on.

params.label: Empirical acceleration
params.what: Constant extra acceleration in radial/transverse/normal axes, for experiments.
params.how: Leave off unless testing the sensitivity to unmodelled forces.

params.label: Empirical radial
params.what: Constant radial acceleration.
params.how: 1e-8 m/s^2 shifts a LEO orbit by metres per day.

params.label: Empirical transverse
params.what: Constant transverse acceleration.
params.how: 1e-8 m/s^2 shifts a LEO orbit by metres per day.

params.label: Empirical normal
params.what: Constant normal acceleration.
params.how: 1e-8 m/s^2 shifts a LEO orbit by metres per day.

params.label: POEORB reference orbits
params.what: Precise orbit products used only for display and comparison (overlay on the globe, error plot). Never used to compute a run.
params.how: Add them to see how far the forecast is from the precise orbit.

params.label: Measured attitude (PROQUA)
params.what: AUX_PROQUA quaternion files for the box-wing model.
params.how: Only used when Shape = Box-wing and Attitude = Measured.

params.label: Earth orientation file
params.what: IERS finals2000A or EOP C04 file (polar motion and UT1-UTC).
params.how: Strongly recommended: without it UT1-UTC and polar motion are taken as zero, which costs metres to tens of metres in the Earth-fixed frame.

params.label: Space weather file
params.what: CSSI file with solar flux F10.7 and geomagnetic Ap history.
params.how: Recommended for NRLMSISE-00. Without it the constant values below are used.

params.label: JPL DE440 file
params.what: Planetary ephemeris for exact Sun/Moon positions.
params.how: Needed only when Sun/Moon ephemeris = DE440.

params.label: Gravity field file
params.what: ICGEM .gfc gravity model (e.g. EIGEN-6S, EGM2008).
params.how: Optional; the bundled EGM96 (to degree 70) is the default.

params.label: F10.7 (constant)
params.what: Daily solar radio flux at 10.7 cm, a proxy for the Sun's heating of the thermosphere. Used when no weather file is given.
params.how: Solar minimum ~70, moderate ~150, maximum 200-250.

params.label: F10.7 81-day mean (constant)
params.what: Centred 81-day average of F10.7.
params.how: Usually close to the daily value outside flares.

params.label: Ap (constant)
params.what: Daily geomagnetic index; storms heat and expand the atmosphere.
params.how: Quiet ~5, unsettled ~15, storm 50-400.

params.label: Weather after cutoff
params.what: How solar and geomagnetic drivers are treated after the cutoff when a weather file is present.
params.how: Persist (cutoff-safe) holds F10.7 at its cutoff value and uses the forecast Ap below. 'Use file' reads actual later values: retrospective only.

params.label: Forecast Ap
params.what: Geomagnetic level assumed after the cutoff (storms cannot be forecast days ahead).
params.how: 5-15 for a nominal forecast; try 50+ for a stressed scenario.

params.label: EOP after cutoff
params.what: Earth orientation after the cutoff.
params.how: Persist holds the cutoff values (cutoff-safe); 'Use file' reads later values (retrospective).

params.label: Absolute tolerance
params.what: Dormand-Prince 5(4) per-step position error target.
params.how: 1e-10 (default) is converged for metre-level work; 1e-8 runs faster with millimetre-level loss.

params.label: Relative tolerance
params.what: Per-step relative error target.
params.how: 1e-12 default; 1e-10 for speed.

params.label: Max step
params.what: Largest allowed integration step.
params.how: 30 s default keeps drag and eclipse transitions well resolved; 60-120 s is faster.

params.label: Min step
params.what: Smallest allowed step.
params.how: Leave at 1e-3 s.

params.label: State source
params.what: Where the starting state comes from.
params.how: Typed: enter it. OEM/POEORB: pick a file; the state nearest the epoch below (or the first) is used.

params.label: State file
params.what: OEM or POEORB file holding the initial state.
params.how: Pick from the catalog or browse.

params.label: Epoch (UTC)
params.what: Epoch of the typed state, or the epoch to pick from a file.
params.how: For files, blank = first state.

params.label: Frame of typed state
params.what: Reference frame of the typed position/velocity.
params.how: ITRF for states from POEORB/GNSS, EME2000/GCRF for inertial states.

params.label: Position X
params.what: Initial position component.
params.how: Metres in the frame above.

params.label: Position Y
params.what: Initial position component.
params.how: Metres in the frame above.

params.label: Position Z
params.what: Initial position component.
params.how: Metres in the frame above.

params.label: Velocity X
params.what: Initial velocity component.
params.how: Metres per second in the frame above.

params.label: Velocity Y
params.what: Initial velocity component.
params.how: Metres per second in the frame above.

params.label: Velocity Z
params.what: Initial velocity component.
params.how: Metres per second in the frame above.
